new.title: Photograph the Palais de l'Isle on the Thiou canal
new.desc: A fortified house on a small island in the Thiou canal, built in the 12th century. It served as a prison until the 19th century, was classed a historic monument in 1900 and now holds a small museum on the city's history. Its ship-like shape is the most photographed view of the old town.
new.tip: Best light is in the morning from Pont Morens or Quai de l'Île. Entry to the museum is paid; the exterior view is free.
new.q: Palais de l'Isle, 3 Passage de l'Île, Annecy

new.title: Climb up to the Château d'Annecy and its museum
new.desc: The restored castle above the old town was the residence of the Counts of Geneva in the 13th and 14th centuries. It was a military barracks until 1947, was bought by the city in 1953 and has been a classed monument since 1959. Today it houses a museum of regional art and the Observatoire régional des lacs alpins.
new.tip: Take the ramp from Rue du Château for views over roofs and lake. Check the museum's current opening hours before going.
new.q: Musée-Château d'Annecy, 1 Place du Château, Annecy

new.title: Cross the Pont des Amours at the lake's edge
new.desc: Officially the Passerelle du Jardin public, this footbridge over the Canal du Vassé links the Jardins de l'Europe and the Pâquier lawn. Locals call it the Pont des Amours after the legend that a couple who kiss at its midpoint stay united for life. The first municipal project for a bridge here dates from 1836.
new.tip: Come at dusk for the lights, or early morning to avoid crowds. It is free and always open.
new.q: Pont des Amours, Quai Napoléon III, Annecy

new.title: Walk the Jardins de l'Europe by the lake
new.desc: A lakeside park on what was once marshland outside the town walls, turned into a promenade in 1602 by Duke Henri de Genevois-Nemours. Plane trees, lawns and exotic species line the path from the old town to the Pâquier. Boat piers for lake cruises are right alongside.
new.tip: Free all year and good with children. Sit by the water with a view of the Semnoz and the Pont des Amours.
new.q: Jardins de l'Europe, Quai Napoléon III, Annecy

new.title: Visit the Basilique de la Visitation above Annecy
new.desc: A church on the Crêt du Maure built between 1909 and 1930 to plans by Alfred-Henri Recoura and consecrated in 1949. It contains the golden bronze sarcophagi of Saint Francis de Sales and Saint Jane de Chantal, founders of the Visitation order in 1610. The 72 m bell tower carries a 38-bell carillon.
new.tip: Free entry; the walk from the centre takes about 12 minutes uphill. The bell tower opens only on certain days, so call ahead.
new.q: Basilique de la Visitation, 11 Avenue de la Visitation, Annecy

new.title: Step inside Annecy's Cathédrale Saint-Pierre
new.desc: A former Franciscan chapel consecrated in 1535, mixing Gothic and Renaissance elements. It became a cathedral in 1822 when the Diocese of Annecy was split from Chambéry and has been a monument historique since 1906. It is the seat of the diocese and a calm stop in the old town.
new.tip: Free and usually open during the day; dress respectfully. It is a short walk from the Palais de l'Isle.
new.q: Cathédrale Saint-Pierre, Rue Jean-Jacques Rousseau, Annecy

new.title: Admire the 15th-century fresco in Église Saint-Maurice
new.desc: A Gothic Dominican church built from 1422 to the early 16th century after Cardinal Jean de Brogny founded a convent here. It holds a carved early 18th-century pulpit and an exceptional mid-15th-century funerary painting of Philibert de Monthoux. It was classed as a national monument in 1957.
new.tip: Entry is free and the church is open daily. The canal running beneath the church is a good photo spot.
new.q: Église Saint-Maurice, 1 Rue Saint-Maurice, Annecy

new.title: Follow the Canal Saint-Dominique under the old town
new.desc: A branch of the Thiou that leaves the main canal near Église Saint-François and runs under houses and churches before rejoining the Vassé canal near the cathedral. Its 19th-century mechanical sluice gates still sit on Quai Perrière. This is the canal network that earns Annecy its 'Venice of the Alps' nickname.
new.tip: Start at Pont de la Halle and wander toward Pont Perrière on foot. Free, and best early before the shops fill the lanes.
new.q: Canal Saint-Dominique, Quai Perrière, Annecy

new.title: Relax on the Pâquier lawn beside the lake
new.desc: A landscaped promenade of seven and a half hectares on the lake shore, also known as the Champ de Mars. Local tradition says Count Bernard VI de Menthon gave much of the land to the town's children in 1613, and the city bought the remaining plots from the 17th century. The tourist office and the Bonlieu theatre stand on its edge.
new.tip: Free and open all year. It hosts the Fête du Lac and other big events, so the grass can be closed off at those times.
new.q: Le Pâquier, Avenue du Petit Port, Annecy

new.title: Take in the Mont Blanc panorama from the Semnoz
new.desc: The Semnoz plateau rises to about 1,700 m above Annecy, with a 360-degree view over Lake Annecy, the Aravis and Bauges ranges, and Mont Blanc on clear days. A viewing table identifies the peaks from the Crêt de Châtillon. It is reached by the D41 road from the city.
new.tip: Go on a clear day and early; the D41 is a winding drive of about 45 minutes. The SIBRA bus line 6 runs to the Semnoz base stop.
new.q: Station du Semnoz, Route du Semnoz, Annecy

new.title: See bells made at the Musée Paccard in Sévrier
new.desc: The museum of the Paccard bell foundry, which was set up in 1984 in Annecy-le-Vieux and moved to Sévrier with the foundry in 1989. The family firm dates from 1796 and has cast more than 120,000 bells. Guided workshop tours show the craft, with bell casting on Thursdays by reservation.
new.tip: Reserve ahead for the guided tour or a casting day. The museum is at 215 route de Piron, a short ride from Annecy on the lakeside cycle path.
new.q: Musée Paccard, 215 Route de Piron, Sévrier

new.title: Visit the old Paccard foundry at the Abbaye, Annecy-le-Vieux
new.desc: The foundry moved here from Quintal between 1854 and 1857 to be near the new railway and cast bells in a wood-fired oven until 1989. The Abbaye building is now a contemporary art exhibition centre and a memorial to the town's rural and industrial past.
new.tip: Check the exhibition calendar before you go. It is a short bus ride from the centre of Annecy.
new.q: Abbaye et ancienne fonderie Paccard, 15 bis chemin de l'Abbaye, Annecy-le-Vieux

new.title: Taste chocolates at Au Fidèle Berger
new.desc: A chocolate maker, pastry shop and tea room founded in 1917 or 1918 on Rue Royale in the old town. It is listed by Gault&Millau among the artisans of Haute-Savoie. Local sweets and Savoyard pastries sit beside the bonbons.
new.tip: Try the house chocolates and ask for the local specialities. It gets busy at weekends.
new.q: Au Fidèle Berger, 2 Rue Royale, Annecy

new.title: Order a tartiflette or fondue at Le Fréti
new.desc: A cheese-focused restaurant in vaulted stone cellars at 12 rue Sainte-Claire with a cheese shop on the ground floor. It serves fondues, raclettes and aged-cheese tastings made from raw-milk farm cheeses. Guides single out its tartiflette and the tartibleu version with blue cheese.
new.tip: Reservations are strongly advised, especially on weekends. It is open daily for lunch and dinner.
new.q: Le Fréti, 12 Rue Sainte-Claire, Annecy

new.title: Dine at Brasserie Brunet, a Bib Gourmand brasserie
new.desc: A brasserie on Rue de la Poste listed by the Michelin Guide with a Bib Gourmand for good-value cooking. The regional tourism page lists menus of about 29 to 47 euros and a children's menu. It serves traditional French dishes.
new.tip: Book ahead for dinner. It closes one week in January and one in May according to older listings, so check hours.
new.q: Brasserie Brunet, 10 Rue de la Poste, Annecy

new.title: Scoop artisan ice cream at Glacier des Alpes
new.desc: An ice cream shop at 16 rue Perrière, started in 2019 by an ice cream enthusiast and consistently praised by reviewers. A free tasting scoop is a recurring detail in reviews. It sits on the arcaded street along the canal.
new.tip: Eat your cone on the Pont Perrière. Opening is generous in summer, shorter off-season.
new.q: Glacier des Alpes, 16 Rue Perrière, Annecy

new.title: Share a Savoyard fondue at Chez Mamie Lise
new.desc: A hearty, nostalgic restaurant on Rue Grenette with kitschy alpine-chalet decor. It serves Savoyard staples such as fondue and tartiflette. Reviews are mixed on the food but praise the old-town atmosphere.
new.tip: Book ahead in the evening. Sources list slightly different addresses, so follow the map pin.
new.q: Chez Mamie Lise, Rue Grenette, Annecy

new.title: Lunch at the Bistrot du Port in Sévrier
new.desc: A traditional-cooking bistrot by Sévrier's harbour on Lake Annecy, open year-round. It is a place to eat lake fish and local dishes by the water in summer and winter. It is listed by the regional tourism board.
new.tip: Take the lakeside bike path from Annecy and arrive for a late lunch. Reserve for summer weekends.
new.q: Le Bistrot du Port, Route du Port, Sévrier

new.title: Dine with a lake view at Black Bass, Sévrier
new.desc: A bistronomic restaurant in Sévrier with a view over Lake Annecy. Adult menus run between 38 and 70 euros for 2026 according to the tourism listing. It is one of several Sévrier tables that serve fish from the lake.
new.tip: Book ahead for terrace tables on summer evenings. Ask which fish is on the seasonal menu.
new.q: Restaurant Black Bass, 921 route d'Albertville, Sévrier

new.title: Try fondue at Le Chalet on Quai de l'Évêché
new.desc: A traditional Savoyard restaurant on the quai de l'Évêché that opened in 2025. Diners mention the fondue and a cosy dining room. It is one of the newer options in the old town.
new.tip: Reserve ahead for evenings. The terrace faces the canal in good weather.
new.q: Le Chalet Restaurant, Quai de l'Évêché, Annecy

new.title: Eat bistronomic cooking at Bleu 1801, Veyrier-du-Lac
new.desc: A bistronomic restaurant on the shore of Lake Annecy at Chavoires in Veyrier-du-Lac. It is listed by the regional tourism board.
new.tip: Check opening days before you go, as lakeside restaurants here are often seasonal.
new.q: Bleu 1801, Chavoires, Veyrier-du-Lac

new.title: Book a table at Le Bouillon in central Annecy
new.desc: A modern-cuisine restaurant in the centre of Annecy that appears with a Michelin Guide Plate in a 2026 listing. It is one of the Michelin-listed tables in the city.
new.tip: Reserve ahead; the Michelin listing comes from an aggregator, so confirm current status.
new.q: Le Bouillon, Annecy

new.title: Cruise Lake Annecy from the Quai Napoléon III
new.desc: Croisières des Alpes, operated by the Compagnie des Bateaux du Lac d'Annecy, runs about one-hour tours of the lake from the quai near the Jardins de l'Europe. It has five boats and also offers full-day trips. Sailings run from about 1 April to 31 October.
new.tip: Tickets are sold at the quai; confirm timetables on the operator's site, as sailings end in autumn.
new.q: Croisières des Alpes, Quai Napoléon III, Annecy

new.title: Cycle the lakeside Voie Verte from Annecy to Sévrier
new.desc: The flat, car-free bike path runs along the lake's western shore from the Pont de la Halle in Annecy, about 5 km to Sévrier where the Voie Verte begins. Bikes can be rented at Roul' ma Poule in Sévrier, about 200 m from the path.
new.tip: Rental from about 10 euros per hour in 2026. Ride in the morning for fewer crowds.
new.q: Roul' ma Poule, 251 Route du Piron, Sévrier

new.title: Hike up Mont Veyrier for a lake panorama
new.desc: A demanding, technical walk to a famous viewpoint above Lake Annecy, often combined with Mont Baron. It can start from the Petit Port in Annecy or from Veyrier-du-Lac. Some guides advise against it for young children because of exposed sections near the top.
new.tip: Wear proper shoes and check parking and access before you go; some car parks are reported closed.
new.q: Mont Veyrier, Chemin du Mont Veyrier, Veyrier-du-Lac

new.title: Swim at the Plage des Marquisats
new.desc: A free grass beach near the city centre with a snack bar, toilets and disabled access. Lifeguards are on duty in high season and the city opened its first inclusive beach here in July 2025. A nautical centre rents equipment.
new.tip: Dogs are not allowed. Bring a towel; parking is nearby but busy in summer.
new.q: Plage des Marquisats, Annecy

new.title: Swim at the Plage d'Albigny in Annecy-le-Vieux
new.desc: A free beach in Annecy-le-Vieux with a sandy lake bed and gentle slope, suited to small children. Floating chairs are provided for people with reduced mobility. Lifeguards watch it from late June to August.
new.tip: Supervision hours differ between sources; check on arrival. Out of season swimming is allowed without a lifeguard.
new.q: Plage d'Albigny, Annecy-le-Vieux, Annecy

new.title: Browse the old-town market on Rue Sainte-Claire
new.desc: The market is held on Tuesdays, Fridays and Sundays all year around Rue Sainte-Claire. It stretches to Place Sainte-Claire with extra stalls along the canal. Local cheese, charcuterie and produce are sold.
new.tip: Hours are roughly 7 to 13, so go early. Free to enter.
new.q: Marché de la vieille ville, Rue Sainte-Claire, Annecy

new.title: Watch the Fête du Lac fireworks over the bay
new.desc: A show of about 70 minutes with fireworks, water jets, lights and music, held on the first Saturday of August in the Albigny bay. The 2026 edition was on 1 August with the show 'L'Âme du Monde'. Viewers gather on the Pâquier, Albigny, Veyrier-du-Lac and boats.
new.tip: Dates for next year should be confirmed with the tourist office; claim a spot on the shore early or book a boat.
new.q: Baie d'Albigny, Fête du Lac, Annecy

new.title: Catch films at the Annecy International Animation Festival
new.desc: Created in 1960 and annual since 1998, the festival takes place in early June, with Bonlieu as its main screening venue. The 2025 edition ran 8 to 14 June and the Cristal award for best feature went to Arco.
new.tip: Check annecyfestival.com for exact dates and tickets each year; accreditation and tickets sell out early.
new.q: Bonlieu Scène nationale, 1 Rue Jean-Jaurès, Annecy
